To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Nusselt numbers for the constant wall heat flux and the constant wall temperature boundary conditions are different for the same nanoparticle volume fraction.

the Nusselt numbers for the thermally developing flow of nanofluid in N-sided polygonal microchannels increase by increasing the nanoparticles volume fractions and by increasing the duct aspect ratio.
the heat transfer rate of Al2O 3 -water nanoﬂuid through regular polygonal ducts enhances with the increase in volume fraction of the nanofluid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a semi-analytical method to solve the fully developed hydrodynamic flow and the thermally developing flow of nanofluid in N-sided polygonal channels.
the development of a new approach for the solution of the governing equations of the hydrodynamical and thermally developing flows of Al 2O 3 -water through polygonal ducts.

developing a semi-analytical method for solving the fully developed and developing flow and heat of Al 2O 3 -water through N-sided regular polygonal ducts with constant wall temperature and constant wall heat flux boundary.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heat transfer enhancement is more pronounced in the polygonal ducts with larger number of sides.
the heat transfer enhancement is strongly dependent on the duct geometry and the boundary conditions.
the heat transfer enhancement in nanofluids is more significant for the thermally developing flow than that in hydrodynamically developing flow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heat transfer in the nanofluid flow through the N-sided polygonal channels is significantly enhanced with respect to the base fluid flow.
the proposed method can be employed to solve various engineering problems with the desired accuracy and efficiency.
the present study can be used as a reference to design heat exchangers for the nanofluid flow through polygonal ducts and can provide a better understanding of the heat transfer in such geometries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat transfer rate is significantly improved in the case of polygonal ducts as compared to circular ducts.
the heat transfer in polygonal ducts can be improved by choosing the appropriate duct geometry.
the Nusselt numbers in the thermally developing region are larger than those in the thermally fully developed region.
